rationale_bullets: Weigman returns off a career year: 74.4/437, 2,705 (65%, 25-9) + 700 rush/11 TD, #5 B12 rating, Texas Bowl MVP - with his first healthy offseason AND first repeat coordinator (Nagle yr 2).
The room behind him is unique: the #1 overall recruit (Henderson) may take packages; Carney (Cuse) adds a third layer.
The scout's line is attributed: 'a stud. Tough, gritty, winner... they'll run the hell out of him.'
62 = solidly above average: proven P4 production + dual continuity, efficiency a notch under elite.
Connors (76.6/337; 977 + 254 rec) graduated - but the replacement is scheme-native: Hughes ran for 1,378 + 1,401 in Fritz's own Tulane offense before a buried 70-yard year at Oregon.
Depth is proven: Butler (75.5/104), Sanford (2024 leading rusher, back from ACL). PS: '3-headed monster... all block well.'
52 = above average: the Hughes projection carries coach-continuity evidence; the burial year and ACL return are the risk.

key_players.name: Makhi Hughes
key_players.evidence: 2,779 yds over 2Y for Fritz at Tulane; 70 yds at Oregon LY

rationale_bullets: A 1st-team All-B12 WR1 returns: Thomas (79.2/397 - 966/12); the 2025 offense funneled 141 catches to him + Koziol vs 45 for everyone else.
Koziol (78.9/322, FBS TE-high 74 rec) left for the NFL, but the swap is verified: Overmyer (76.2/212 - 'NFL-caliber,' Athlon) + Walker (69.4/419; 1,714 over 2Y at OSU).
Depth thickens (Young 8 starts, Athlon-bold Broussard, Turner/Tounkara, 4* Bushnell); PS: 'more depth and playmaking options than in recent seasons.'
58 = above average: elite piece + verified replacements, no proven third target.
The baseline is bad (27th-pctile as-played, #106 P6 Run Push) and the returning tackles are the weakest verified pieces (Ebosele 54.5/957, Agnello 62.5/773).

But the incoming trio is the best OL tape haul of our round: Hurst (80.7/934, 1st-tm AAC - 'one of the better guards in the portal'), Boswell (77.0/819, 1st-tm MAC), Terrill (76.8/734, All-MAC) - each better than anything they lose.
The trajectory is attributed: 135->178 rush and 33->19 sacks year-over-year; PS: 'should continue to improve.'
46 = fringe-below-average: three verified all-league adds pull a bottom-third line toward the middle; the tackles cap it.
An 84th-pctile as-played unit loses exactly its top two: Walls (77.4/779, sack leader) and Allen (73.3/679, #1 tackler).
The rotation that returns is real: Laufau (72.1/696), Mack (69.6/515, 5 sk), McCutchin (68.2/379), Parker - plus adds Porter (Oregon 4*, 66.3/245), D.Thomas (OkSt), All-Ivy Egodogbare.
PS: 'need that crop of big DL to emerge... depth and talent mix to be as good or better' - conditional, attributed.
55 = above average: quality rotation, top-end departed.
Both 2025 flankers gone (Garner 65.2/665 grad; Platt 67.9/357 -> TT); Fotu (67.2/543, bold) anchors the middle.
Adds carry production pedigree with modest grades: Yates (62.5/371 at Ole Miss; 115 tkl at Marshall '24), Malone (64.8/342 WKU).
PS: 'the first 3 are rock solid but the team is still looking for a fourth ILB.' LB caution rule: grades and framing roughly agree - average-minus room.
48 = fringe-average.

rationale_bullets: Three bold returning starters (James 77.8/562 - all-league; Allen 76.3/676; Webb 65.9/812, all 13 starts) from an 88th-pctile unit - Athlon calls it 'the unit's strength.'
The losses are elite (L.McCutchin 78.2/796 + W.Brown 83.9/490, both All-B12) and the depth thinned by graduations.
Adds are targeted: White (Tulane All-AAC, 68.5/654) at nickel, Mayo (SFA, 4 INT - 'played well against Houston in the opener'), 4* Melvin early.
60 = top-40: three proven starters + verified nickel vs two elite exits.
The 6-1 one-score season leaned on K Sanchez (21-26, three game-winners) - and he's gone, with a three-way battle behind (experienced Yoakam vs #1-prospect Noel vs Dimas).
P Dougherty returns (44.1 career-best avg, but 39.2 net and a #84-88 STR history); RM Mews gone.
SPEC 72.4 = 40th pctile; PS: 'may take a step back.' 42 = below average.
